title: Something that I’m using AI to code but..
author: Valentinevandal1986
selftext:
So I’m working on a plugin currently that is maybe useful to some others and potentially we might be able to crack it if we think about it together. 

My idea was to figure out a way to incorporate autonomous robots movement research and development with something like Nvidia Motionbricks to basically create a pathfinding system that can analyze its environment and adapt on the fly. 

My goal is to create a system that can move like a humanoid through its environment and chase down the player character while incorporating angle, momentum, inertia and balance into its movement system. Think ultimate tag ai edition. I’m currently running simulations on my gpu training it but if anyone has any expertise in this area I’m open to suggestions and collabs

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
...what advantage would that system have over A\* pathfinding? 

It seems like a very cycle-intensive way of accomplishing nothing more than what can already be achieved by a well-established algorithm.

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: It will allow for more realistic humanoid movements without needing to program the states. The ai will actively scan its environment, plot out its course based on the realistic human abilities and available routes and dynamically adjust using Motionbricks as the bridge to control the motion and animation automatically. Characters would adjust gait, stance and their overall movements based on the terrain they can physically move through instead of using nav mesh and canned animations

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Yes, I understand that, but the end result is still 'thing moved from A to B, with an associated animation'. 

You are basically arguing that by making this process more complex, it is better for some reason, and you haven't explained why it is better, only why it is more complicated.

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body:
Currently an engineer has to program where an npc can go. My system you don’t need any of that. You drop an npc in an environment and it figures out movement by itself based on its capabilities.

Its strongest potential differentiator is the combination of:

Autonomous affordance discovery: recognizing useful opportunities for movement without manually assigned traversal labels.

Capability-aware planning: understanding that two characters may have different routes through the same environment.

Multi-action chaining: discovering routes requiring combinations of jumps, climbs, vaults, drops and eventually swinging.

Momentum-aware reasoning: treating speed, approach direction, orientation and physical state as part of route feasibility.

Motion independence: selecting a physically meaningful traversal strategy without depending on a particular animation library or neural model.

Let’s say you wanted to create an enemy with unpredictable movements, this would instead of making program in areas it can move, let it automatically calculate based on its limitations of its own body, the best and most efficient path through an environment. Think ultimate tag level parkour but without having to program any of the routes. The goal would be to drop an AI with this programmed into a completely unknown obstacle course and have it be able to navigate to any location you set but instead of pre programming routes.

Think about Atlas robot and how it uses a movement controller to adjust and predict where its body is going to be in the future, so it can plot a route across obstacles and terrain. Now put that into an npc who doesn’t need gyros and physical sensors, it reads the code. There’s way less “noise” for the system to deal with in the virtual environment. Instead of telling the AI what routes it can take it will discover them on its own. That being said the constraints of a humanoid skeletal structure will serve as a basis for its movement so climbing a 15 foot wall shouldn’t be possible but climbing a 7 foot wall would be. 

Since the system controls and informs the animations and vice versa, things like combat and movement through an environment would look unique each time as it will take into account the characters footing and momentum. You could have a large enemy with big swings and it wouldn’t be entirely predictable where their sword might strike with each swing. The wind up would look similar but taking into account their forward momentum, footing and inertia the swing might end up going a bit more left or right, so it would create more dynamic gameplay and less predictable paths. Like an enemy getting stuck under you and just pacing wouldn’t happen because if you could do it, the AI should be able to solve for reaching you, no matter where you go, unless you have more capabilities than the AI. I’m trying to build an AI that can hunt down a player character given the exact same controller as the player with the same physical constraints. I’m going for Matrix/Assassins Creed/Prince of Persia style fluid movements and I need the AI to be able to pursue the player and do all the exact same movements and abilities that the player can do and adapt on the fly as the player moves around the environment without having to program in specific areas that is allowed to move in. The player would be using the same system for calculating movement, it would just be player controlled instead of AI controlled

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
>Currently an engineer has to program where an npc can go. 

  
...No, you don't. You just set up the A\* pathfinding algorithm, give the NPC movement rules, and it will explore the map emergently as long as the rules interface correctly with the terrain. You do not have to set up bespoke movement routes. 

And your system, as described, cannot skip the part where you set up the interface between the NPC behaviour and the terrain it is navigating.

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: It’s not emergent. You can layer it with other things to get emergent style behaviour but my system is different. It calculates on the fly its own environment. So if you have a 4ft tall character, it won’t be able to navigate the same way a 6ft character would vs a 10ft tall character. It’s taking into account the balance of the model as well, so it’s balancing by itself, figuring out what paths are available in any environment it’s dropped into, then using that information and predictive motion controllers to keep the model upright and moving, while at the same time using motionbricks to make the motions look believable and convincing. So you won’t get characters sliding on the terrain, they will have physical contact and adjust on the fly. Right now the characters aren’t using the physical surface of the level geometry to move, it’s using navigation to tell it what’s solid, what’s a safe space to walk, where can’t it walk. Like maybe there’s a steep hill/wall. If the AI has enough space, it could take a running start at it, if the space is constrained, it might not be a viable path. So it will intuitively decide where it can and can’t walk given its read of the level geometry and if you place a waypoint or have it track a player controlled character it will follow and move to the locations by itself using realistic human looking movements based on balancing, angle, momentum and inertia. Making for dynamic stuff like the ability to jump off a shield if it presents a surface that’s angled correctly, run on a wall with enough momentum, run up and backflip off a wall, jump between a moving larger character and the level geometry ie shadow of the colossus, dragons dogma. All that stuff uses pre designed movements that look nearly identical every time they play out, I’m trying to build an entirely dynamic system that works for any character and any environment

replies.author: Valentinevandal1986
replies.body: Yeah, I’m basically trying to build something that communicates with Motionbricks to use it as a bridge to solve the animations for autonomous movement. The Pathfire system would identify routes, ask motion bricks for the animations to match it, then motion bricks would inform the system as well based on where it can realistically move. It wouldn’t need programming beyond giving it the specific physical parameters of its body then it would use that to calculate where in space it can move through a system similar to robotic vision. It could adapt to changing environments, variables on the fly is the goal so changing level geometry would still be possible and it would just recalculate its route
